name: AI News
blurb: Daily AI news from the publishers who broke it, split into headline coverage of the field and vendor announcements from the companies building it. Every story links to the original source, and any claim quoted in our coverage is cross-referenced against the laws, lawsuits, companies, tools, papers, and people already tracked in this atlas.

domains.name: AI Headline News
domains.blurb: The day's most consequential AI stories across law, policy, research, safety, and society, curated from 34 vetted feeds. Each item carries the original publisher link and a note on how it connects to the bills, cases, and frameworks tracked elsewhere on this site.

domains.name: AI Vendor News
domains.blurb: Product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements from the AI vendors themselves. Each item links to the vendor's original announcement and cross-references the company's profile in our AI Companies directory where one exists.

domains.name: This Week in AI
domains.blurb: A weekly record of what moved in AI policy and litigation, permalinked by ISO week.

domains.name: AI Historical Timeline
domains.blurb: From the 1940s to the present: Turing, the perceptron, expert systems, backpropagation, deep learning, AlexNet, transformers, and what followed.

domains.name: When AI Goes Wrong
domains.blurb: Logged harms from deployed AI systems, catalogued by the AI Incident Database and carried here with our own reading of what failed. An incident is one reported event, not a pattern; the recurring failure modes underneath them are catalogued separately in AVID. Headlines published in another language are translated, and the original stays on the source link.

reading.body:
Of 564 pages in this AI news archive, 548 are curated headline coverage and exactly one is vendor news, so the record is built from law, policy, research, and safety rather than company announcements.

The archive is lopsided by design. Headline coverage runs to 548 pages drawn from 34 vetted feeds and spans law, policy, research, safety, and society. Vendor news, which covers product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements, occupies a single page. The weekly policy and litigation record adds 15 pages, one per ISO week. The historical timeline is live but holds no pages at all.

For AI specifically, the implication is about where documented change is coming from. The material assembled here is weighted toward bills, cases, and frameworks, and each item is cross-referenced against them. Company announcements are present but negligible in volume. A reader tracking what moved in AI would find the legal and policy record far denser than the product record.

The counts do not measure the world. A page is an editorial unit, not a story or an event, so 548 pages does not mean 548 consequential developments. One vendor page may mean the section is new rather than that vendors announced little. Nothing here covers compute, power, datacenters, or capital spending, so no conclusion about the grid or about AI scaling follows from it. The empty timeline is an unfilled section, not a claim about history.
